content.text:
This structure is ponatinib: an imidazo[1,2-b]pyridazine joined through an alkyne to a tolyl amide, with a CF3-substituted aryl bearing a 4-methylpiperazinylmethyl group.

**Imidazo[1,2-b]pyridazine.** The five-membered ring contains a bridgehead N, C3 (bearing the alkyne), a CH, an N and the fusion carbon. The six-membered ring contains the bridgehead N, an N, and three CH carbons that close back to the fusion carbon. Written as SMILES: C#Cc1cnc2cccnn12.

**Central benzene ring.** The alkyne-bearing carbon is adjacent to the methyl-bearing carbon. The amide carbonyl sits meta to the alkyne, which gives: Cc1ccc(C(=O)N...)cc1C#C...

**Right-hand aryl ring.** The NH-bearing carbon is C1. Going around the ring from it, the next carbon is CH, then the CF3-bearing carbon, then the CH2N-bearing carbon, then CH, then CH back to C1. Written as SMILES: c1cc(CN2CCN(C)CC2)c(C(F)(F)F)cc1 attached at the NH carbon.

**Check of the right-hand ring against the drawing.** The ring atoms are N-attached C (1025,945), top-left CH (1030,835), top CH (1127,783), the CH2-bearing carbon (1220,843), the CF3-bearing carbon (1215,953) and the bottom CH (1118,1005). The NH carbon is therefore bonded to a CH, which leads to the CH2-bearing carbon, and to another CH, which leads to the CF3-bearing carbon. This puts CF3 meta to the amide N and the CH2 group para to it, which matches the SMILES above.

SMILES: Cc1ccc(C(=O)Nc2ccc(CN3CCN(C)CC3)c(C(F)(F)F)c2)cc1C#Cc1cnc2cccnn12
